issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes using snake_case names (e.g. 'lecture_name', 'number_of_inscribed_students') but the constructor and all methods reference camelCase field names (e.g. 'lectureName', 'numberOfInscribedStudents'). This causes undefined field references and will not compile, and it also deviates from the attribute names specified in the problem statement UML (camelCase). Students consulting the solution or trying to compile it will be blocked by these name mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute names consistent between declarations and usage and align them with the UML/case convention. For example, declare fields as private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents; private int numberOfGuestStudents; private int numberOfLecturers; private int numberOfTutors; and keep the constructor and methods using these camelCase names. Alternatively, update all usages to match the declared snake_case names, but prefer camelCase to match the problem statement and Java conventions.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML use camelCase attribute names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The solution implementation declares these attributes using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) but the constructor and all methods reference the camelCase identifiers (e.g., this.lectureName). This creates a direct mismatch that breaks the conceptual mapping for students and causes compilation errors in the solution. Students cannot reliably map the UML-specified attribute names to the implemented fields, and the internal inconsistency in the solution adds extraneous cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Make identifier names consistent with the UML and template expectations. Rename the private fields in the solution to use camelCase: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors (or alternatively change all constructor parameters and methods to match snake_case). Prefer aligning with the problem statement/UML (camelCase) so constructor, getters, setters and toString consistently reference the same field names.
